source.title: Orthogonal Graph Neural Networks
source.authors: Kai Guo; Kaixiong Zhou; Xia Hu; Yu Li; Yi Chang; Xin Wang

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation affecting the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own comparisons showing that deeper GNNs lose classification performance and that Ortho-GConv partly prevents that degradation. These are related classification outcomes, but the paper does not measure training classification error from random initialization on the datasets specified by the claim.
record.gate_note: The study tests graph neural networks and depth-related classification performance, but reports test accuracy rather than training classification error. Its results therefore do not directly test the near-zero training-error claim. Rows record the study's own depth comparisons and signal measurements; cited results from other studies are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study uses orthogonal initialization and weight constraints to develop Ortho-GConv, evaluating test accuracy and signal stability. It does not measure training-error degradation, initialization-dependent learning speed or trainable depth, or any other version's specified outcome. Its gradient and signal measurements alone do not establish V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors argue that unstable forward and backward signaling from feature transformation is a primary cause of GNN performance degradation, especially in shallow models, and conclude that Ortho-GConv stabilizes signaling and improves node and graph classification performance.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies graph neural networks and proposes hybrid initialization, orthogonal transformation and orthogonal regularization; it does not use the claim's CIFAR convolutional-network training recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Model depth; whether feature transformation is removed or Ortho-GConv is applied; the orthogonal iteration count T affects reported accuracy and training time.

fits_no_version.finding: On Cora, vanilla GCN test accuracy deteriorates with depth, whereas removing feature transformation maintains accuracy through 100 layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Feature transformation contributes to depth-related test-performance degradation in the evaluated GCN setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Ortho-GCN improves full-supervised Cora test accuracy over vanilla GCN at 2, 4 and 8 layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The combined Ortho-GConv intervention improves test accuracy in these GCN comparisons.

fits_no_version.finding: Vanilla GCN embedding distances approach zero beyond 20 layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Deep vanilla GCNs exhibit embedding collapse in the evaluated Cora setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Ortho-GConv keeps signal magnification near one and yields comparable gradient norms across eight layers, whereas vanilla GCN exhibits amplification and vanishing gradients.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The combined orthogonal initialization, transformation and regularization intervention improves measured forward and backward signal stability in GCNs.

record.problems: The reported classification outcomes are test accuracy rather than training error. The study's graph benchmark settings differ from the CIFAR and network settings in the claim. Some flattened table values make row assignment uncertain; the Cora 8-layer original GCN value is inconsistent with the text's broad depth-degradation statement.
record.rows_left_out: The supplied Table 2 is flattened, and its dataset/backbone mapping cannot be reliably reconstructed for all listed values; retained only the Cora GCN entries that the table order supports. No training-error rows are reported.

untested.parts: Training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including random or corrupted labels.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth-dependent training error, longer-training controls, identity shortcuts, and the stated initialization and normalization exceptions.

Initialization-dependent learning speed and trainable depth, activation matching, and orthogonal-versus-Gaussian comparisons. The initialization ablation reports test accuracy rather than these outcomes.
Recovery, curvature dynamics and divergence relative to learning-rate stability thresholds.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and tolerated learning rates, and comparable training without normalization using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Differences in measured outcomes are not scope limitations on the supplied versions. Accordingly, neither the proposed V3 limits_scope label nor the V4 supports label is warranted.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test training classification error, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, or corrupted/random labels.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment or width sweep.

Tests graph neural networks on graph datasets, not batch-normalized convolutional networks on ImageNet or CIFAR-10. Does not compare identity shortcuts; Ortho-GConv is a different stabilizing method. It does not report training error or longer-training comparisons.

Tests an orthogonal feature transformation and reports signal magnification, gradient norms and classification accuracy, but does not compare the activation-matched initializations or the plain tanh/CNN settings named in the version.
No learning-rate stability-limit or sharpness sweep.
Does not test batch normalization, its training-speed or learning-rate effects, or Fixup.

rows.subject: GCN
rows.operation_detail: Measured node classification accuracy as depth increased on Cora.
rows.value: Accuracy drops quickly when depth is enhanced to 8.
rows.locator: Figure 1(d); Forward and Backward Steadiness Analysis
rows.note: The paper describes the accuracy decline in text; this is test accuracy, not training error.
rows.check: Figure 1(d) measures test accuracy in GCNs, not V3's training-error degradation in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks.

rows.subject: GCN w/o W
rows.operation_detail: Removed the feature transformation module and measured node classification accuracy across depths.
rows.locator: Figure 1(d); Forward and Backward Steadiness Analysis
rows.note: A comparison condition relevant to depth degradation; it is not an identity-shortcut model.
rows.check: Stable test accuracy after removing feature transformation does not measure V3's training-error outcome or identity-shortcut comparison.

rows.subject: GCN
rows.operation_detail: Compared full-supervised node classification accuracy for original GCN and Ortho-GConv-equipped GCN at different depths.
rows.note: This result is test accuracy; it does not establish training error or the plain-network versus identity-shortcut comparison in V3.
rows.check: The Table 2 values are correctly assigned to the 2-layer Cora GCN comparison, but measure test accuracy. The value belongs to Ortho-GCN and the baseline to vanilla GCN; this is a proposed-method performance comparison.

rows.subject: GCN
rows.operation_detail: Compared full-supervised node classification accuracy for original GCN and Ortho-GConv-equipped GCN at different depths.
rows.note: The baseline value is difficult to reconcile with the paper's general depth-degradation narrative; accuracy is not training error.
rows.check: The Table 2 values are correctly assigned to the 8-layer Cora GCN comparison and agree with depth degradation from the 2-layer baseline of 85.77%. The record's inconsistency concern is unfounded. These are test accuracies comparing Ortho-GCN with vanilla GCN.

rows.subject: GCN
rows.operation_detail: Compared full-supervised node classification accuracy for original GCN and Ortho-GConv-equipped GCN at different depths.
rows.note: Test accuracy comparison; does not measure the version's training-error outcome.
rows.check: The Table 2 values are correctly assigned to the 4-layer Cora GCN comparison, but measure test accuracy comparing Ortho-GCN with vanilla GCN.

rows.subject: GCN
rows.operation_detail: Measured node classification accuracy and graph smoothness as depth increased.
rows.value: Metric D approximates to zero once L > 20.
rows.locator: Figure 1(d); Forward and Backward Steadiness Analysis
rows.note: Smoothness is not classification error; paper says GCNs fall into random prediction in this setting.
rows.check: Embedding smoothness does not measure V3's training error. The stated size of 8 layers is also wrong for this result, which concerns depths greater than 20.

rows.subject: Ortho-GCN
rows.operation_detail: Compared signal magnification across model depths with vanilla GCN.
rows.baseline: Vanilla GCN's Msig rises quickly with depth.
rows.value: Msig constrained around value 1 for models of different depths.
rows.locator: Figure 1(a); Steadiness Study of Our Model
rows.note: Measures a signal-stability metric, not classification error.
rows.check: Signal magnification measures forward stability, not V3's training error or V4's initialization-dependent learning speed or trainable depth. This result spans multiple depths rather than a single 8-layer model.

rows.subject: GCN
rows.operation_detail: Measured gradient norms by layer during training.

conditions.value: initial training phase and after hundreds of epochs

rows.value: Decreasing tendency at initial layers; after hundreds of epochs, all gradients at different layers were vanishing.
rows.locator: Figure 1(b); Illustration of model steadiness metrics
rows.note: The paper describes vanishing gradients in vanilla GCN; it does not give numerical gradient values in the text.
rows.check: Vanishing gradient norms in vanilla GCN do not establish an initialization-dependent difference in training speed or trainable depth.

rows.subject: Ortho-GCN
rows.operation_detail: Measured gradient norms by layer after adding Ortho-GConv.
rows.baseline: Vanilla GCN gradients decrease across layers and vanish during training.
rows.value: Gradient norms comparable for the different layers within an 8-layer model.
rows.locator: Figure 1(c); Steadiness Study of Our Model
rows.note: The paper reports this as evidence that Ortho-GConv maintains backward gradients.
rows.check: Comparable gradient norms under the combined initialization, transformation and regularization intervention do not establish V4's initialization-dependent learning speed or trainable depth.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: GCN depth comparisons and Ortho-GConv on graph-classification benchmarks
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports declining accuracy with increased depth and improved accuracy after Ortho-GConv, but measures test accuracy on graph benchmarks rather than training error or identity shortcuts (R1, R3, R4, R5).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Vanilla GCN and Ortho-GCN gradient measurements
reader_labels.reason: Vanilla GCN gradients are described as vanishing, while Ortho-GConv yields comparable gradient norms across layers in an 8-layer model (R8, R9).
